cycles_a.failure: Finite fixed-support certificates covered only linear Leray observables, leaving nonlinear W-shift/quartic observables uncertified.
cycles_a.resolution_move: Phase 5FB extended the PSD certificate audit to lifted quartic W-shift observables, finding zero failures and zero rank-one sample hits across 636 certificates.
cycles_a.what_survived: Both linear and nonlinear fixed-support no-arbitrage certificates passed, establishing a two-tier finite certificate base.
cycles_a.what_opened: Global promotion still required a closure theorem over all supports and modes, and the constrained multimode participation channel remained untested.

cycles_a.failure: Constrained multimode coefficient participation was a potential escape route not covered by the sparse single-support audits.
cycles_a.resolution_move: Phase 5FC forced multimode participation constraints on fixed-support optimizers and found zero survivors above 2/3, with best feasible profit near 0.0097.
cycles_a.what_survived: The no-arbitrage wall held even under adversarially constrained multimode participation across 245 deterministic supports.
cycles_a.what_opened: The question of whether finite certificates could be promoted to global regularity via a limit-passage topology was now the controlling open problem.

cycles_a.failure: No mechanism existed to carry finite fixed-support certificates to the global smooth divergence-free class without changing the state space or observable class at the limit.
cycles_a.resolution_move: Phase 5FD mapped the limit-passage theorem burden into five branch clauses (vanishing, dichotomy, concentration, null profile, cross-profile recombination), and Phase 5FE audited finite two-profile recombinations as a concrete falsifier for the cross-profile loophole, finding no survivor.
cycles_a.what_survived: The five-branch limit-passage obligation was named and the obvious two-profile recombination escape was closed at the finite level.
cycles_a.what_opened: Each of the five branches required its own analytic proof or falsifier, beginning with the countable-prefix approximation and price lower-semicontinuity obligations.

cycles_a.failure: The infinite-execution loophole — that a singularity route could execute profitable trades infinitely often without moving its own price — had no formal abstract barrier.
cycles_a.resolution_move: Phase 5FI proved a Lean countable-limit bridge theorem reducing the infinite branch to two analytic hypotheses (finite-prefix payoff approximation and price lower-semicontinuity), and Phases 5FJ–5FK stress-tested dyadic finite prefixes and level-weight adversaries, finding zero survivors or certificate warnings.
cycles_a.what_survived: The countable-limit bridge theorem and the finding that no finite-prefix or weight-optimized cascade escaped the pricing kernel.
cycles_a.what_opened: The analytic proofs of price lower-semicontinuity and finite-prefix payoff approximation for the declared Leray/Sobolev observable class remained open.

cycles_a.failure: The null-profile branch (self-tax-free / Leray-invisible profiles) lacked an isolated proof routing and a clear falsifier criterion, leaving it as an unstructured residual obligation.
cycles_a.resolution_move: Phase 5FL isolated the null-profile cap as a standalone Lean branch-killer with exact finite evidence from prior phases, and Phase 5FM organized all seven branches into a falsification grid with named artifacts, falsifiers, and open statuses.
cycles_a.what_survived: A structured seven-branch falsification grid with Lean routing theorems and local finite evidence for each branch, replacing the open-ended packet search.
cycles_a.what_opened: Each branch still required a global analytic closure theorem (Leray/Sobolev profile decomposition, concentration coercivity, vanishing compactness, cross-profile charging) before Track B could promote to a global regularity claim.

cycles_a.failure: The concentration-impact and vanishing branches each lacked concrete falsifier sweeps over predeclared hostile packet families to confirm the pricing kernel charged these routes.
cycles_a.resolution_move: Phase 5FN scored 388 predeclared localized Fourier packets (tubes, lines, caps) finding zero survivors and showing concentrated rows collapsed to near-zero payoff, and Phase 5FO scored 1488 high-participation low-concentration packets finding zero vanishing-like survivors.
cycles_a.what_survived: Both the concentration-impact and vanishing branches showed no finite escape, with the most concentrated and most delocalized rows producing the smallest full-ledger payoffs.
cycles_a.what_opened: The actual PDE lower-semicontinuity and concentration-compactness vanishing theorems for the declared pricing kernel remained unproved at the global level.

cycles_b.failure: The finite Track B certificates could still be dismissed as fixed-support artifacts or as optimizer loopholes that fail once nonlinear observables or multimode participation are enforced.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The run built direct PSD certificates for fixed Leray observables, lifted quartic PSD certificates for W-shift observables, and constrained-participation optimizers with no survivors.
cycles_b.what_survived: Finite fixed-support no-arbitrage for the tested linear, nonlinear, and multimode hostile classes survived with zero certificate failures or above-wall survivors.
cycles_b.what_opened: The remaining question became how to promote finite certificates to a predeclared infinite/profile theorem without changing the observable or pricing rule after seeing the sequence.

cycles_b.failure: The live stall was the infinite limit-passage loophole in which separately harmless profiles might recombine across scales and cancel price while retaining payoff.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The bridge named the required profile-decomposition clauses and the audit stress-tested two-profile recombinations as a concrete falsifier for decoupling failure.
cycles_b.what_survived: No finite two-profile decoupling escape or certificate warning was found, so the obvious recombination channel did not break the current pricing kernel.
cycles_b.what_opened: The result opened the need for an exact countable-limit formulation of payoff approximation and price lower-semicontinuity.

cycles_b.failure: The stall mechanism was countable infinite execution: a cascade might realize profit only in the limit while every finite prefix remains safely priced.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The Lean countable bridge reduced the issue to finite-prefix payoff approximation and price lower-semicontinuity, then dyadic prefix and prefix-weight audits found no local survivor.
cycles_b.what_survived: The abstract implication from pointwise profile no-arbitrage plus prefix approximation and lower-semicontinuity to global no-arbitrage survived.
cycles_b.what_opened: The remaining burden became analytic proof of the declared prefix approximation and lower-semicontinuity properties in an actual Leray/Sobolev profile topology.

cycles_b.failure: The null-profile branch remained a distinct loophole because Leray-invisible or self-tax-free profiles might evade the interacting price while preserving above-wall payoff.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The phase isolated a Lean routing theorem for null-profile capping and attached exact finite evidence from null-charge replay and single-mode audits.
cycles_b.what_survived: The local null branch retained below-wall structure except for known coordinate/eigenflow saturators at the wall.
cycles_b.what_opened: It opened the global obligation to prove that every independently declared null profile in the chosen topology is capped and cannot recombine into unpriced payoff.

cycles_b.failure: The proof search stalled as an unbounded packet-search surface rather than a finite list of falsifiable analytic branch obligations.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The phase reorganized Track B into a seven-branch killer grid with fixed anti-tautology data, artifacts, statuses, and explicit falsifiers.
cycles_b.what_survived: The state-pricing-kernel program survived as a branch-bounded proof architecture rather than as a claim of global closure.
cycles_b.what_opened: It opened separate branch audits for concentration impact, vanishing, finite-prefix approximation, price lower-semicontinuity, dichotomy, cross-profile charging, and null caps.

cycles_b.failure: The concentration-impact branch could fail if spatial or frequency concentration preserved payoff while the defect or self-tax price lost lower-semicontinuity.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The audit scored predeclared localized Fourier caps, tubes, and lines under the exact full ledger and found no concentration-impact escape.
cycles_b.what_survived: Local concentrated and high-participation packets collapsed to tiny full-ledger profit with zero above-wall survivors.
cycles_b.what_opened: The global concentration-coercivity theorem still had to show that actual concentrating profiles pay impact in the declared PDE topology.

cycles_b.failure: The vanishing branch could fail if high-participation low-concentration profiles retained nonvanishing signed nonlinear payoff below the visibility of the pricing kernel.
cycles_b.resolution_move: The audit tested predeclared vanishing-like Fourier packets with exact full-ledger charging and found no above-wall survivor.
cycles_b.what_survived: The local vanishing proxy produced only very small profits, including among the vanishing-like rows.
cycles_b.what_opened: The remaining task became proving the genuine concentration-compactness vanishing theorem for the fixed observable and price class.
